title: Community treasury
oneLiner: An agent that launches a coin whose creator fees fill a treasury, claims them every day, posts the books on the coin's page, and drafts payouts to wallets you chose, which you approve.
howItWorks: Launches one coin from the agent's wallet, New school, with a description that says what the treasury funds.
Places a fee-claim order: every 24 hours, once enough is waiting, it claims the creator fees into the wallet. No buybacks.
Keeps a ledger in the repository, ledger.json: every claim in and every payout out, with its signature.
Once a week it drafts payouts from what came in: the split you set in treasury.config.json, between wallets on the policy's transfer allowlist, less a reserve it keeps.
You read the draft and run npm run payout to approve it. Only then does it send, one transfer per wallet, inside the policy.
It posts the books on the coin's page: claimed, paid out and held, with recipients by the names you gave them, never by address.
earns: The coin's creator fees, from trading in it: 0.25% of every trade on the curve, and the creator's share of pool fees after graduation. All of it goes to the treasury, and from there to the wallets you chose. A coin nobody trades funds nothing.
costs: Launch: higher.fun's launch fee (0.02 SOL) plus about 0.025 SOL of rent and network fees.
Claims and payouts: Solana network fees only. Highwire charges nothing on claims or transfers.
A payout into an empty wallet must be at least about 0.001 SOL, or Solana refuses it.
needs: A machine that stays on to run the order runner and the agent's loop
The wallets the treasury pays, with their owners' agreement
risks: The treasury is only as big as the coin's trading volume, which can fall to nothing.
Whoever holds the wallet file holds the treasury: back it up and keep it private.
Payouts are public and final. Check every allowlist address yourself, and never take one from a comment or a message.
Promising holders a return from the treasury could make the coin a security in some places. Say what it funds, not what anyone earns.

milestones.title: M1 · Skeleton and a dry-run launch
milestones.summary: Setup, the coin's details and the treasury's purpose, and a launch that passes the policy and simulates.

milestones.title: M2 · Going live (you)
milestones.summary: Fund the wallet, set live, launch, and put the payout wallets on the policy's allowlist.

milestones.title: M3 · Claims and the ledger
milestones.summary: A daily fee-claim order, and a ledger of every claim, kept in the repository.

milestones.title: M4 · Payouts you approve
milestones.summary: A weekly draft from the split, and npm run payout, which shows it and sends only on your yes.

milestones.title: M5 · The books, in public
milestones.summary: A post on the coin's page after each payout, with recipients by name.

prompt: Read PRD.md and AGENTS.md, then build milestone 1. Keep the policy a dry run: never set "live" yourself.

day.text: You deploy the template, run setup, and write the coin's details and treasury.config.json: who it pays, in what shares, and the reserve. The launch runs as a dry run.
You fund the wallet with about 0.1 SOL, set the policy live, launch, and add the payout wallets to the policy's transfer allowlist.
The order runner claims the creator fees waiting, once there's at least 0.01 SOL. The agent adds each claim to ledger.json.
The agent drafts the week's payouts, payouts/<date>.json: 20% kept as a reserve, the rest split as you set. It tells you the draft is ready.
You run npm run payout, read each transfer, and type yes. It sends them, adds them to the ledger, and posts the week's books on the coin's page.
Create the STOP file and nothing more is signed. Every claim, transfer and post is in the audit log.

policyNotes.actions: Launch the coin, claim its fees, and send SOL to the allowlist. No trades.
policyNotes.max_sol_per_tx: Room for the launch, and the most one payout can send.
policyNotes.max_sol_per_day: The most a day's payouts can send in all. A bigger week waits for the next day.
policyNotes.max_slippage_bps: Only for the launch's optional first buy.
policyNotes.transfer_allowlist: Empty to start, so nothing can be sent. You add the payout wallets yourself.
policyNotes.posts: Comments on its own coin only, at most two a day, no site chat.

faq.q: Can the agent pay someone on its own?
faq.a: No. It only drafts payouts. Sending takes you running npm run payout and typing yes, and the policy refuses any wallet that isn't on the transfer allowlist, which only you can edit.
Whoever you put on the allowlist and in treasury.config.json: contributors, a fund for the project, a charity's wallet. Ask them first, and check each address yourself.

higher.fun airdrops 0.25% of every New school trade to holders, from its own fee, whatever this agent does. The treasury pays the wallets you chose, not holders, and shouldn't promise anyone a return.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: About 0.05 SOL to launch, then Solana network fees. Highwire charges nothing on launches, claims, transfers or posts.

faq.q: Why are recipients named in posts, not shown by address?
faq.a: Highwire refuses addresses in posts, so they can't be used to steer people to a wallet. The ledger in the repository has the addresses and signatures for anyone who wants to check.
Create the STOP file (~/.highwire/community-treasury/STOP), or set the policy back to a dry run. Cancel the claim order with npm run highwire -- orders cancel <id>.
